name: Velocity into filter cutoff / filter-envelope amount
goal: Make pads/synths expressive with velocity→filter: set lowest desired cutoff with filter EG amount at 0, raise EG amount (with sustain) for max brightness on hard hits, then map velocity so soft hits stay darker—know your synth’s polarity (many brighten on hard hits; some Moog-style reduce brightness as velocity sens rises).

source.title: Adjusting Velocity to Filter Cutoff – Synth Clips 7 – Daniel Fisher

prerequisites: Synth with low-pass filter, filter envelope amount, and velocity→filter (or velocity→EG amount) routing

inputs.name: darkest_cutoff
inputs.description: Cutoff with EG amount 0 = softest intended tone

outputs.name: expressive_filter_pad
outputs.description: Velocity-sensitive filter brightness on pad/synth voice

steps.action: Init: single bright oscillator (e.g. saw), 24 dB/oct LP, resonance off, filter EG amount 0, keytrack 0. Sweep cutoff to hear range (can go below fundamental).
Set cutoff to the darkest tone you want when the envelope is not pushing (EG amount still 0).
With sustain-full filter envelope, raise EG amount until held notes reach maximum intended brightness (hard-hit ceiling).
steps.expect: Bright ceiling set via EG amount

steps.action: Enable velocity→filter (or velocity→filter EG amount). Learn polarity: typical = harder = brighter; some synths (Subsequent/Sub 37 style) increase velocity sens to make soft playing darker instead—strategy reverses.
steps.expect: Soft vs hard hits change brightness predictably

steps.action: Play slow soft velocities while raising velocity amount until darkest desired soft tone; verify fast hits still hit the bright ceiling. Trim EG amount if hard hits are too bright; resonance exaggerates the difference.
steps.expect: Natural soft→bright response without accidental extremes

verification: Soft velocities darker than hard velocities (per chosen polarity)
EG amount 0 defines dark floor; EG amount sets bright ceiling
Resonance (if used) does not make response unusable
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI (Ableton/Vital/Serum/VAST/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth vendors named in the source video.
Portable for Traveler/Web Audio: velocity curve → filter cutoff and/or filter-envelope depth.
